about: THE CHAIN house_debt (Design/content/CHAINS.md; the page is Design/content/chains/house_debt.md): the 1,920 pennies (it was 480 until 7 Oct 2026) owed to the count of Dorestad for the boat, from the split tally on the first morning (21 June 793) to the count's friendship, his enmity, Saint Martin's protection or the rival's dam head. Fourteen cards, four endings (flags ch_house_debt_end_friend, ch_house_debt_end_enemy, ch_house_debt_end_st_martin, ch_house_debt_end_sold). Cast (Design/content/spine.json): the count is cast.folcbert, the steward cast.hartwin, the rival skipper cast.thiadbod, the widow cast.thiadburg, the moneyer cast.sigimar, the bishop cast.hamacar (the only historical person). Cards with weight 0 come only when another card schedules them or names them in 'then'; their 'when' says when they belong. The engine has no verb that changes the debt itself, so a payment is a cost in silver and the flags ch_house_debt_owed (480 or 0) and ch_house_debt_cleared say where the tally stands (see 'needs' in the page). Words: Data/writing/chain_house_debt.json. A draft for the user to overwrite.

cards.note: Step 1, the start: Dorestad, the first call of a new game (21 June 793). Weight 40 so that it is all but sure to be the first card drawn: it is the game's opening. Steward: cast.hartwin. Sources: trade_rules.json start (480 d, creditor.count); Design/DECISIONS.md no. 10 (480 d by Michaelmas); spine thread counts_day. No count of Dorestad is named in the 790s (Design/content/dossiers/dorestad.md 8): the count is invented. Lending at interest forbidden to all: Admonitio generalis 789 c. 5 (MGH Capit. I no. 22; de.wikipedia 'Zinsverbot') (?). The split tally is the game's device, recorded only from about 1100 (LATER).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and year < 796 and not flag.ch_house_debt_1 and not flag.lender_opening
cards.title: The tally
cards.intention: The count's steward waits at the dam head with a hazel stick split down its length: 1,920 pennies lent for the boat, due at Michaelmas.

options.label: Take your half and say you will be there
Leave twelve pennies for the count's table, as the custom is
Say the boat was never worth eight pounds

memory.take: took his half of the tally
memory.gift: left a gift for the count's table
memory.argue: argued the price of the boat

cards.note: Step 2: Dorestad, about twenty days after the tally (scheduled by step 1). The warning of the chain's danger: the rival buys other men's tallies. Rival: cast.thiadbod; widow: cast.thiadburg; Sibrad is an invented oarsman (Sib- + -rad, names_placeholder.json). The English cloth: the ports of Charles and Offa were shut to each other's merchants from about 789 to 796 (spine thread black_stones; Gesta abbatum Fontanellensium c. 12), so the order is a risk he passes on.
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_1 and not flag.ch_house_debt_2
cards.title: A friend on the bank road
cards.intention: Thiadbod, who has the best dam head in Dorestad, comes along the bank road to wish you well. His sister, the widow Thiadburg, watches from her storehouse door.

options.label: Take his order for English cloth
Thank him and take no favours
Ask him, before his sister, whose sticks hang in his storehouse

memory.take_order: took Thiadbod's order and his favour
memory.ask_tallies: asked Thiadbod about the bought tallies

cards.note: Step 3: Dorestad, the first reckoning, due from Michaelmas (29 September) 793 (scheduled by step 1; it opens at the first mooring at Dorestad after the day). Count: cast.folcbert, in the hall at De Geer (a lord's seat by the digs; that it is the count's is our guess (?): dossier dorestad 2). 'On the day' is to the end of October 793. Branches: 3a paid, 3b a year's grace for the boat's work (spine flags db_extension, db_service), 3c the boat pledged. Sources: Michaelmas as a feast: Council of Mainz 813 c. 36 (spine calendar); the loss on the Weser: chronicle_793.json 793-summer-rustringen-defeat (Annales regni Francorum, revised, 793); the famine: 793-great-famine; no more than was lent: Admonitio generalis 789 c. 5 (?). Paying on the day uses the deed kept_commission, the nearest there is.
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_1 and not flag.ch_house_debt_3
cards.title: The count's day
cards.intention: The reckoning. In the count's hall the steward lays the two halves of the hazel stick together on the board, and the count looks at you over them.

options.label: Count out what you still owe, on the day
Count out what you still owe, late
Ask until next Michaelmas, and offer the boat's work for it
Lay the mooring rope on the board: the boat is his pledge

memory.pay_day: paid the debt for the boat on the day
memory.pay_late: paid the debt for the boat, late
memory.grace: asked a year and offered the boat's work

cards.note: Step 4: Dorestad, about Martinmas 793, in the great famine (scheduled by step 3, which warns of it in the count's own words). A side step for every road: who is fed. Branches: 4a to the count at his price, 4b on the dams at the hungry price, 4c shared with the church door, 4d none. Steward: cast.hartwin; the priest serves Saint Martin's church above Dorestad (the Upkirika, given to Utrecht in 777: dossier dorestad 2). Sources: the famine of 793: chronicle_793.json 793-great-famine (Annales Laureshamenses, Chronicon Moissiacense, Annales Mosellani); the just price of wheat, four pennies the measure, and lords to keep their people from starving, were set at Frankfurt only in June 794 (MGH Capit. I no. 28 c. 4; 794-06-01-frankfurt-prices), so here the price is the count's own. Six and twelve pennies the sack are the game's (goods_793.json wheat 6 d).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_3 and not flag.ch_house_debt_4

priest.note: the priest of Saint Martin's church above Dorestad; invented

cards.title: The hungry winter
cards.intention: The count's steward stands on the bank with a list of the households on the count's land that have eaten their seed corn. He looks into every hold that comes up the river.

options.label: Sell the count four sacks at his price
Sell four sacks on the dams at the hungry price
Carry two sacks to the church door and sell him the other two
You have no corn to spare

memory.to_count: sold the count wheat at his price in the hungry winter
memory.to_dams: sold wheat at the hungry price
memory.to_poor: gave wheat at the church door

cards.note: Step 5: Dorestad, after midsummer 794 (scheduled by step 3 for those who still owe): the king's new heavy penny, and whether a tally of 1,920 pennies is paid by tale or by weight. Branches: 5a by tale (the count has near a third more silver than he lent: the flag ch_house_debt_tale_taken is a true grievance later), 5b by weight, 5c left to Michaelmas. Moneyer: cast.sigimar. Sources: the new denarii to be taken everywhere, and fifteen shillings from a free man who refuses them: Frankfurt, June 794, c. 5 (MGH Capit. I no. 28; Fordham sourcebook 'Monetary Regulations of the Carolingians', read 4 Oct 2026; chronicle_793.json 794-06-frankfurt-new-denier); the light penny of about 1.3 g until 793/4 and the monogram penny of about 1.7 g after: dossier dorestad 4; 480 x 1.3 / 1.7 = 367. Whether old debts were to be paid by tale or by weight no source says: the dispute is ours (?). The riddle is Symphosius 91, money (riddles_793.json).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_3 and flag.ch_house_debt_owed and not flag.ch_house_debt_5 and year >= 794
cards.title: The king's new penny
cards.intention: The mint at Dorestad is striking the king's new penny, broad and heavy. The count has heard the law from Frankfurt read, and has sent for every man whose stick still hangs in his hall.

options.label: Pay what you owe by tale in the new pennies, and see the stick burned
Have the moneyer weigh out what you owe in new pennies, about three for every four by tale, and pay that
Say you will answer at Michaelmas

memory.pay_tale: paid the tally by tale in the new pennies
memory.pay_weight: paid the tally by the moneyer's weight
memory.stand: let the tally stand till Michaelmas

cards.note: Step 6: Dorestad, Michaelmas 794 (scheduled by step 5; it comes a second time if the bishop is asked and gives nothing). The rival offers the count the full tale for the stick. Branches: 6a matched and paid, 6b the widow's surety (spine flag db_surety; the lasting cost is the flag ch_house_debt_widow_share), 6c to the bishop, 6d sold (spine flag db_bought; the ending is step 14). Rival cast.thiadbod, widow cast.thiadburg. Sources: the host of autumn 794, two armies into Saxony: chronicle_793.json 794-autumn-sintfeld (Annales regni Francorum 794). The sale of a debt and the widow's lending on goods are the spine's (thread counts_day); a third share of a venture for the lender follows the shape of the later commenda, thin in the north (Design/economy_and_trade.md 2.9) (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_5c and flag.ch_house_debt_owed and year >= 794
cards.title: The stick for sale
cards.intention: The count is making ready to ride with the host, and he does not mean to leave an open stick behind him. Thiadbod stands at his elbow. On the board lie your tally, a purse and a cask of wine.

options.label: Match the bid: what you owe, in new pennies, and the stick is burned
Take the widow's surety: a quarter of the debt now and a third of three cargoes
Say the bishop will hear of it, and go down to Utrecht
Let him sell it

memory.pay: matched Thiadbod's bid and paid by tale
memory.bishop: went to the bishop about the tally
memory.sold: let the tally be sold to Thiadbod

cards.note: Step 7: Traiectum (Utrecht), a day's row below Dorestad, autumn 794 (scheduled by step 6). Bishop: cast.hamacar, historical (bishop about 790 to 806 in the bishops' list; nothing else is known of him, so his words are invented). Branches: 7a Saint Martin's man (the ending is step 13), 7b the letter and the weight paid through the bishop's clerk (spine flag db_surety; the deed carried_letters), 7c nothing, and back to step 6. Sources: Saint Martin's men on the banks at Dorestad owe the king's officers nothing, nobody may lodge in their houses or take their goods at death: Louis the Pious, 18 March 815, confirming older grants (Oorkondenboek Sticht Utrecht I no. 56; dossier dorestad 4); that this already held in 794 is assumed (?). Usury forbidden to every Christian: Admonitio generalis 789 c. 5; the definition, more asked back than was given, is Nijmegen 806 c. 11 (MGH Capit. I no. 46) (?). The stone fort and Saint Martin's church: dossier traiectum 1-2.
cards.when: moored and port.id = traiectum and flag.ch_house_debt_6c and not flag.ch_house_debt_7 and year < 807
cards.title: Saint Martin's man
cards.intention: Inside the old stone fort at Utrecht the bishop hears you between the hours, a deacon with a book beside him. He has waited a long time for a complaint against the count of Dorestad that he could put in writing.

options.label: Kneel, and put your hands between his
Ask for the letter and pay the debt by weight to his clerk
Thank him and go back up the river as you came

memory.letter: took the bishop's letter on usury and paid the weight

cards.note: Step 8, a turn on the long road (the tally closed, the house its own): Daventre, April to August of 794 to 799, drawn on a call there. The stores of the host that goes into Saxony each year. Branches: 8a served (ch_house_debt_served_host; on a failed chance the boat is kept unpaid, ch_house_debt_pressed, a true grievance later), 8b supplied, 8c refused. The count's man is invented. Sources: Daventre on the host's road east, grain and salt meat bought up each May (spine thread saxon_end; dossier daventre 1); 794 two armies: chronicle_793.json 794-autumn-sintfeld; 795 to the Elbe and more hostages than before: 795-summer-bardowick-campaign; 797 the king's ships hauled over land and by river into Saxony: 797-summer-ships-into-saxony (Annales Guelferbytani 797). A penny a load is the game's.
cards.when: moored and port.id = daventre and flag.ch_house_debt_long and not flag.ch_house_debt_8 and not flag.ch_house_debt_10 and year >= 794 and year < 800

man.note: the count's man with the stores; invented

cards.title: Stores for the host
cards.intention: Carts and horse lines on the river bank at Daventre, and one of the count's men counting sacks on a wax tablet. The host goes east into Saxony again, and its stores must cross the river and go up it.

options.label: Carry the stores for twelve days
Take his order for salt pork instead
Say the boat has her own summer

memory.serve.success: carried the host's stores and was paid
memory.serve.failure: carried the host's stores and was kept unpaid when the water fell
memory.supply: took an order for the host
memory.refuse: would not carry for the host

cards.note: Step 9, a turn on the long road: Dorestad, whenever she lies there with a falcon aboard (the steward names the wish in steps 1, 3 and 8). Branches: 9a given (ch_house_debt_hawk: with the debt paid on the day it opens the hard road's finale), 9b sold; keeping her sets nothing and the card may come again. Sources: falcons as gifts between the great: goods_793.json falcons; Boniface sent a hawk and two falcons to King Aethelbald of Mercia about 745, and King Aethelberht of Kent asked him for two more (Boniface's letters, Tangl nos. 69 and 105) (?). The king winters at Aachen from 794: chronicle_793.json 794-12-25-aachen-winter. That a white northern hawk reached a Frankish count in the 790s is our own (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_long and hold.falcons >= 1 and not flag.ch_house_debt_9 and not flag.ch_house_debt_10 and year < 806
cards.title: A hawk from the north
cards.intention: The count has come down to the dam head himself, which he does not do. Somebody has told him what sits on the perch in your stern.

options.label: Give him the hawk for the king
Sell him the hawk at the dam's price
Keep her for another market

memory.give: gave the count a hawk for the king
memory.keep: kept the hawk from the count

cards.note: Step 10, the long road's last choice: Dorestad, April to October of 796 to 805, drawn on a call there. The king's man takes the oath and hears wrongs; the merchant speaks for the count (the ending is step 11) or tells how tallies are sold in his hall (step 12). Before 802 the king's man is a poor vassal of the palace and the complaint is only likely to be heard (ch_house_debt_judged or ch_house_debt_unheard); from 802 the envoys are great men and it is sure. Envoy and clerk invented: no envoy to the Dorestad district is recorded. Sources: Charles to Offa, 796: 'traders have due protection within our kingdom ... let them appeal to us or our judges' (tr. in E. P. Cheyney, Readings in English History, Boston 1922, p. 56; chronicle_793.json 796-spring-offa-letter); the oath of every man from twelve years up and the envoys sent to do justice, none 'kept back from the right path of justice by the adulation or the reward of any man': Capitulare missorum generale 802 c. 1-2 (tr. E. F. Henderson 1896; chronicle_793.json 802-spring-oath-of-802); an earlier general oath after the plot of 792: MGH Capit. I no. 25 (?); in 802 the king would no longer send poorer vassals of the palace to do justice, because of gifts: Annales Laureshamenses 802, from memory (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_long and not flag.ch_house_debt_10 and year >= 796 and year < 806 and (hold.falcons = 0 or flag.ch_house_debt_9)
cards.title: The king's man
cards.intention: Strangers sit at the count's own board, sent to take every free man's oath and to hear any man's wrong. The count stands by the door of his own hall, and every tally stick in it lies on the board.

lines.when: not flag.ch_house_debt_served_host and not flag.ch_house_debt_hawk and not flag.ch_house_debt_fed_his_people

options.label: Say the count dealt justly with you
Tell him how sticks are sold in this hall
Tell the emperor's envoys how sticks are sold in this hall

memory.speak_for: spoke for the count before the king's man
memory.complain_early.success: complained of the count and was heard
memory.complain_early.failure: complained of the count and was not heard
memory.complain_late: complained of the count to the emperor's envoys

cards.note: Step 11, an ending: THE COUNT'S FRIENDSHIP (flag ch_house_debt_end_friend), after step 10. Three finales: the ground on the king's bank (unlock_plot_dorestad); a seat among the seven who find judgment (unlock_title_doomsman_dorestad), for a man who fed the count's people, served the host or paid by tale; and the hard road, for the man who paid on the day and gave the hawk: the ground and a charter of toll freedom (unlock_charter_dorestad), which is history changed (changed_dorestad_toll_charter). Sources: seven judgment-finders (scabini) in the count's court: Design/content/peoples/frankish.md 3 (the capitularies; for a Frisian merchant among them (?)); a hen as a yearly due: the polyptych of Irminon (peoples/frankish.md 2); the bolt of silk: the Avar treasure, shared by the king among his great men in 796 (Annales regni Francorum 796; Einhard, Vita Karoli c. 13; chronicle_793.json 796-winter-avar-ring-plundered, 796-autumn-avar-treasure-shared); no layman known free of the tenth at Dorestad: the emperor's own merchants pay it there in 828 (Praeceptum negotiatorum, MGH Formulae imperiales no. 37; dossier dorestad 4) (?).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_spoke_for and not flag.ch_house_debt_end_friend
cards.title: A hen at Michaelmas
cards.intention: The king's man has ridden on. The count sends for you, not to the hall but to the bank below it, where a strip of the king's ground runs down to the water between two dam heads.

options.label: Take the ground on the king's bank
Ask instead for a seat among the seven who find judgment
Ask him to carry your asking to the king: the freedom of the toll

memory.dam_head: took ground on the king's bank from the count
memory.seat: sits among the seven in the count's court
memory.charter: won the freedom of the toll through the count

cards.note: Step 12, an ending: THE COUNT'S ENMITY (flag ch_house_debt_end_enemy; the lasting cost is the flag ch_house_debt_count_enemy), after step 10. Three finales: heard, the king's protection and the palace's carrying (unlock_title_kings_protection); heard, with what was taken given back twofold, for a man who paid by tale or whose boat was kept unpaid; unheard, the bishop's wall at Utrecht (unlock_factor_traiectum). The clerk is the bishop of Utrecht's; invented. Sources: the king's ban of sixty shillings: Lex Ribuaria 65 and the Capitulare Saxonicum of 797 (?); twofold amends: the Lex Frisionum has a thief pay double (title III) (?); a merchant under the king's protection, his ship not to be taken: attested for the emperor's merchants in 828 (Praeceptum negotiatorum), assumed possible a generation earlier (?); bishop and count disputing fines: the spine (cast.hamacar). Under the engine an order is posted at the port of the card, so the palace's orders are delivered at Dorestad; the bishop's wants are price shocks at Traiectum.
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and (flag.ch_house_debt_judged or flag.ch_house_debt_unheard) and not flag.ch_house_debt_end_enemy

clerk.note: a clerk of the bishop of Utrecht; invented

cards.title: The count's enemy
cards.intention: The hall is quiet. The king's man has finished with the sticks, and the count has come back in from the door to hear what is said of him at his own board.

options.label: Take the king's man's letter and carry for the palace
Take the letter, and ask back twofold what was taken from you
Go down to Utrecht, and trade from behind the bishop's wall

memory.letter: took the king's protection against the count
memory.restitution: had back twofold what the count took
memory.utrecht: went over to the bishop's side of the river

cards.note: Step 13, an ending: FREEDOM BOUGHT ANOTHER WAY, as Saint Martin's man (flag ch_house_debt_end_st_martin; the lasting cost is the flag ch_house_debt_st_martins_man: he carries for the church when asked and is judged in the bishop's hall), after step 7 at Traiectum. The church pays the count; the reward is the freedom of the toll on Saint Martin's bank at Dorestad (unlock_charter_dorestad). This is the ending nearest to what the sources show: such men stood on those banks. Sources: Oorkondenboek Sticht Utrecht I no. 48 (8 June 777: the church above Dorestad and its bank) and no. 56 (18 March 815: the men of the church on the banks free of the king's dues, lodging and seizure), by the dossier dorestad 2, 4; the bishop's wants, wax, wine and letters: the spine (cast.hamacar); hands between hands: Tassilo commends himself so in 757 (Annales regni Francorum) (?). Aldhelm's riddle of the scales is in texts_793.json.
cards.when: moored and port.id = traiectum and flag.ch_house_debt_7a and not flag.ch_house_debt_end_st_martin
cards.title: Hands between hands
cards.intention: In the small stone church of Saint Martin, inside the fort at Utrecht, you kneel and put your hands between the bishop's. A clerk writes your name under the names of the saint's other men on the banks at Dorestad.

options.label: Ask what Saint Martin wants carried first
Ask that a clerk teach your house its letters

memory.wax_wine: is Saint Martin's man and carries for the church
memory.school: is Saint Martin's man and asked for letters

cards.note: Step 14, an ending: SOLD (flag ch_house_debt_end_sold; the lasting cost is the flag ch_house_debt_thiadbods_man: a third of what the boat earns is his), after step 6 at Dorestad. The rival holds the tally and does not call it in; the reward is a sworn partner with the best dam head on the river (unlock_partner_thiadbod) and his goods in the hold. With the widow as witness the third cannot be raised (ch_house_debt_terms_witnessed). Rival cast.thiadbod, widow cast.thiadburg; Sibrad invented. Sources: Frisian merchants trading in company: the spine (thread counts_day; the sworn felag by that name is Norse and later (?)); witnesses to a bargain: Frankish and Frisian law prove by witnesses and oath-helpers (peoples/frisian.md 3).
cards.when: moored and port.id = dorestad and flag.ch_house_debt_6d and not flag.ch_house_debt_end_sold
cards.title: Thiadbod's second boat
cards.intention: The count has ridden east with the host. Your hazel stick hangs in Thiadbod's storehouse now, on a peg between two others, and Thiadbod is pouring the wine himself.

options.label: Drink with him and sail as his second boat
Ask the widow to stand witness to the terms first

memory.witness: sails as Thiadbod's second boat, on witnessed terms
